diseases.name: Tomato Early Blight
diseases.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings resembling a target board, primarily on older lower leaves. Leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely.
diseases.causes: Warm temperatures (24-30°C) with high humidity, frequent rainfall, or overhead irrigation.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and resistant tomato varieties.
Practice 3-year crop rotation avoiding Solanaceae family (potato, eggplant, pepper).
Maintain adequate plant spacing (60 cm) for air circulation.
Water at the base of the plant using drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage.
treatment: Organic: Apply copper-based fungicides or Bacillus subtilis spray every 7-10 days.
Chemical: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP (2 g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP (2 g/L) at first appearance of spots.
Remove and safely destroy infected lower leaves (do not compost).

diseases.name: Tomato Late Blight
diseases.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale to dark lesions on leaves, white velvety fungal growth on undersides during wet weather. Stems develop dark greasy lesions.
diseases.causes: Cool, humid weather (15-22°C) with prolonged leaf wetness (fog, heavy dew, rain).
prevention: Destroy cull piles and volunteer tomato/potato plants before planting.
Ensure excellent field drainage and avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Mulch around plant bases to prevent soil splash onto lower stems.
treatment: Organic: Copper oxychloride 50% WP (3 g/L) as a protective barrier spray.
Chemical: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil MZ 2 g/L) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (Sectotin 2 g/L).
Immediately rogue out severely infected plants to prevent rapid field epidemic.

diseases.name: Potato Early Blight
diseases.symptoms: Small brown concentric ring spots on mature leaves, leaf blighting and premature tuber senescence.
diseases.causes: Alternating wet and dry periods, stressed plants with low nitrogen.
prevention: Maintain balanced fertilization with adequate nitrogen and potassium.
Use certified disease-free seed tubers.
Eliminate solanaceous weed hosts (black nightshade).
treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (1 ml/L).
Apply Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide during vegetative stage.

diseases.name: Potato Late Blight
diseases.symptoms: Rapidly expanding water-soaked necrotic patches with light green halo. Tubers develop granular reddish-brown dry rot.
prevention: Plant certified resistant varieties (e.g. Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini).
Hill up soil well over developing tubers to prevent spore washdown.
treatment: Prophylactic spray of Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5 kg/ha).
Curative spray of Dimethomorph 50% WP (1 g/L) + Mancozeb (2 g/L).

diseases.name: Rice Blast Disease
diseases.symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with grayish center and dark reddish-brown margin on leaf blades and neck nodes.
diseases.causes: High nitrogen fertilizer application, cloudy skies, prolonged dew periods.
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer application; apply in split doses.
Maintain proper water level (2-5 cm) in paddy fields.
Treat seeds with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed before sowing.
treatment: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L.
Spray Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2.5 ml/L for organic and bio-management.

diseases.name: Rice Brown Spot
diseases.symptoms: Numerous small circular to oval brown spots with yellow halo all over the leaf blade and grain glumes.
diseases.causes: Nutrient-deficient soils (especially low Potassium and Silicon), drought stress.
prevention: Apply recommended dose of Potash (MOP) and Zinc sulphate.
Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed.
treatment: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (2 ml/L).

diseases.name: Wheat Yellow / Stripe Rust
diseases.symptoms: Yellow to orange-yellow powdery pustules arranged in narrow distinct stripes along leaf veins.
diseases.causes: Cool and moist weather (10-15°C) with morning dew.
prevention: Cultivate rust-resistant varieties like DBW 187, DBW 222, HD 3086.
Timely sowing in November to avoid late-season rust build-up.
treatment: Foliar spray of Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (1.25 ml/L) or Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L).

diseases.name: Cotton Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot
diseases.symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by leaf veinlets, black arm lesions on branches, water-soaked boll spots.
diseases.causes: High humidity (85%) and temperature (28-35°C), wind-driven rain.
prevention: Acid delinting of cotton seeds with commercial sulphuric acid (100 ml/kg seed).
Destroy cotton stubble and crop residues after harvest.
treatment: Spray Streptocycline (100 mg/L) + Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) at 15-day intervals.

diseases.name: Citrus Canker
diseases.symptoms: Raised corky, crater-like lesions surrounded by an oily yellow halo on leaves, twigs, and fruit peel.
diseases.causes: Warm, wet weather, leaf miner injuries providing entry wounds.
prevention: Prune and burn infected shoots during winter before spring flush.
Control citrus leaf miners with Neem oil or Imidacloprid to prevent entry wounds.
treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1% or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (3 g/L) + Streptocycline (1 g / 10 L).

diseases.name: Grape Black Rot
diseases.symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves; berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
diseases.causes: Warm, humid conditions with free moisture on foliage for 6-24 hours.
prevention: Canopy management for maximum sunlight penetration and aeration.
Remove mummified berries and infected canes during dormant pruning.
treatment: Spray Myclobutanil 10% WP or Mancozeb 75% WP before bloom and fruit set.

diseases.name: Healthy Foliage (No Disease Detected)
diseases.symptoms: Vibrant green uniform pigmentation, intact cell structure, absence of necrosis, chlorosis, lesions, or fungal sporulation.
diseases.causes: Optimal agronomic management, balanced soil nutrition, and good environmental conditions.
prevention: Continue regular scouting and balanced NPK fertilization.
Maintain appropriate irrigation scheduling and soil moisture levels.
treatment: No remedial action needed. Maintain preventative crop health care.
